Decision IC: on the 26 days it traded, what it bought ranked against what it sold and left alone by a mean rank IC of 0.043 with the next five days' returns (IC IR 0.37, t = 1.9, within noise).
Holdings IC: the weights it held after each of 50 decision days had a mean rank IC of 0.044 with the next five days' returns (t = 1.6, within noise).
Factor exposures: market 0.34 (t 9.0), size -0.05 (t -0.9), growth -0.34 (t -3.7), momentum 0.09 (t 2.3); together they explain 45% of the daily variation (R²).
Of the -2.2% a year it earned over T-bills (arithmetic mean): market -6.6%, growth +5.9%, momentum +0.7%, size +0.1%; the alpha left is -2.3% a year (t = -0.3, within noise).
Verdict: the exposures account for +0.1% a year of it, and the -2.3% a year left over is not significant: one period of daily returns cannot tell it from luck.
